reckon/mcp.py:_edit_plan_tool (override_wip_limit wired to the MCP surface)

findings.text: the override comment is written on any create whose caller passes a non-empty override_wip_limit, whether or not the project was actually at its limit, so the recorded audit artifact asserts a refusal that never happened. Reproduced at the reviewed head in /tmp/review-probe/probe.log: a project at 1 pending against a limit of 25, created with override_wip_limit="defensive caller", carries the comment body "opened beyond the pending-plan limit of 25 (1 pending): defensive caller"; a project declaring no limit, created the same way, carries "opened beyond the pending-plan limit of None (0 pending): defensive caller" — a literal None in a persisted plan comment. The caller is not told the field is conditional (the tool docstring says only "Pass override_wip_limit=<reason> to open the plan anyway"), so a script or agent that passes it unconditionally writes a false reason onto every plan it creates, and the locked refuse-with-override decision exists precisely for that reason to be true. Gated at the call site as `if create and wip_override:` with limit already in hand (None for an uncapped project), the record should be written only when limit is not None and pending_count >= limit. The repair was falsified in a scratch copy of the head: a red check that a below-limit or uncapped create records no comment fails at the reviewed head for exactly those two reasons (logs/check-unfixed.log) and passes with the call site gated, the over-limit create still recording its reason (logs/check-fixed.log), while the four declared cases stay green (logs/check-fixed-tests.log).

the measurement_module field states the relative path "reckon/mcp.py" where the contract asks for the absolute path the run printed for module.__file__; both gate logs carry the printed value (/tmp/base-reckon/reckon/mcp.py for the base arm, the reviewed worktree's reckon/mcp.py for the head arm), so the fact is recoverable from the evidence layer but not from the field that is supposed to carry it, and a reader resolving the field alone resolves it against their own tree.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified 2 production call site(s): the refusal and override record sit on _edit_plan's create path, and _edit_plan_tool carries the new argument to the MCP surface with the behaviour named in its docstring; no other caller in reckon/ passes create=True, so the create path under test is the one in production use.
item_verdicts.diff: commit 87874436 read against base 11d1f949 adds 360 lines across exactly four files, the four declared write paths: reckon/mcp.py (152 added lines: three read helpers mirroring roadmap's own guard shape, the refusal, the override record, the new argument on both the function and the tool wrapper), docs/state/reckon/project.json (the limit declared beside the horizon), tests/test_pending_plan_limit.py and the evidence fragment; the diff touches no plan and no other path. The skill's documented primary creation route writes plan HTML directly ("Authoring the file directly is the primary path. The MCP tool is an optional version-safety wrapper, not a gate.", reckon-create SKILL.md), so the cap binds the MCP create path only; the reviewed brief named that surface exactly, so the node is correct against its brief, and the gap is recorded under follow_ons for the plan's own goal rather than scored here.
item_verdicts.done_when: every clause of the reviewed brief's measure reproduces independently at /tmp/review-head-reckon (module.__file__ /tmp/review-head-reckon/reckon/mcp.py, cwd /tmp/review-head-reckon): the resource declares pending_plan_limit 25 beside schedule_horizon_sprints and reads 25 on the real project through the new helper; a project with 5 pending against limit 3 is refused with "already holds 5 pending plans, at its limit of 3" naming exactly three plans ranked by impl (0.95, 0.9, 0.85) and the override, and the refused slug's file is absent afterwards; a done-status plan and a plan carrying plan-archived=1 are both excluded from the count (a first probe with the wrong meta name miscounted 6 and named the archived plan first — corrected instrument, parse_meta returns archived=1, count 5); the override lets the create through and the reason lands as a comment; a project declaring no limit is never refused and neither is a limit of 2 with 1 pending; at exactly the limit the create is refused. On the real reckon project the census reads 68 pending over 147 plan rows (77 closed-status, 3 archived, 0 missing impl), matching the velocity view's own 68 in this plan's gate evidence. The four cases in tests/test_pending_plan_limit.py pass when I run them at the head (4 passed, EXIT=0).
item_verdicts.goal: the reviewed node's goal was to refuse creation of a plan beyond the project's pending-plan limit, naming the plans nearest to closing, with a recorded override. §3 of the plan it serves delivers a per-project pending-plan limit in project configuration, enforced at plan creation in the lead-locked refuse-with-override mode, with the refusal naming the three pending plans nearest to closing; the node's brief scoped that enforcement to reckon/mcp.py:_edit_plan's create path and named the exact measure, and the delivered code implements it there with the limit declared in docs/state/reckon/project.json at the locked value of 25, so the goal is delivered in full against its brief and all but the override-recording clause against observed behaviour.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full; status complete, the head and base arms both armed JSON with completed true, matching revisions, no-placeholder commands and log paths, add-failure derivation stated, negative control named with its path and its red-log reading, follow_ons carrying the pre-existing vocabulary failure. Two precision gaps: measurement_module is relative rather than the printed absolute (the second finding below), and measurement_cwd names the head worktree only, which is acceptable because the base arm's scratch-tree cwd is on its own log header.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares reckon/mcp.py, docs/state/reckon/project.json, tests/test_pending_plan_limit.py, the evidence fragment and a figures directory; commit 87874436 touches exactly the four non-figure declared paths and nothing else, no figure was produced and the brief states a figure is not owed where the done-when names no artifact, and no plan or shared index was edited.

justifications.durability: the change is committed at a clean head, its gate arms are pinned to revisions in logs that open with revision, tree, command and the imported module path, the negative control log is persisted and its first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim with the declared FAILED id and EXIT=1, and the guard is fail-closed — the refusal returns before the plan's parent directory is created, which I re-observed as the absent file. What the change does not pin is the false override comment: no case covers a caller passing the override below the limit or on an uncapped project, so the recorded audit artifact can be wrong with nothing failing. The review falsified the repair it proposes in a scratch extraction of the head: with the call site gated on the limit, the red check goes green and the four declared cases still pass.
justifications.evidence: strong and independently reproduced: two full suite arms at named revisions with identical single failure ids, a declared negative control that fails as declared, gate logs whose headers carry the scratch-tree module.__file__ and cwd, and new tests I re-ran green at the head in a scratch extraction; my own probe confirms the refusal sentence, the three-plan ranking, the closed and archived exclusions and the count on the real project, whose 68 pending matches the velocity view's figure in this plan's own gate. The only evidence-layer gap is the relative measurement_module field, which the logs themselves repair.
justifications.fit: the helpers mirror the repository's existing idiom rather than inventing one — _pending_plan_limit is the same None-guard shape as roadmap._schedule_horizon sitting on the same projects[0] row, the closed definition is imported from velocity rather than re-derived, and the refusal is a machine-readable error payload with a human sentence beside it, matching how _edit_plan already returns errors. The commit carries a conventional subject and a body stating the mechanism, no attribution, no plan or sprint identifier in code, comments or message, and the config key is declared beside the horizon key it sits with. The one style departure is _record_wip_override's missing return annotation.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the brief's goal is delivered and verified end to end: creation beyond the limit is refused in the locked refuse-with-override mode, the refusal names the limit, the count, exactly three pending plans nearest to closing ranked by impl, and the override; the override opens the plan and records the reason as a comment; an uncapped project is never refused; pending is the velocity census's own definition imported rather than re-derived, and the real project's count agrees with the velocity view. One clause of the delivered behaviour is wrong: the override reason is recorded even where no refusal occurred, naming a limit the plan never exceeded and, on an uncapped project, a limit of None.
justifications.scope_discipline: the commit is exactly the declared footprint — four paths, all inside the fence, with the plan, the shared index and every other artifact untouched; the node returned its outcome as a manifest landing line and a fragment rather than editing the plan; the one declared path it did not use is a figure directory, and the brief states no figure is owed.
